subject.title: Feature: Built-in pace-aware rate limiting for autonomous agents

question: What pace and admission surface should OpenClaw core own for autonomous agents when provider quota windows are running hot?
rationale: The request adds public config/defaults, provider usage state, status/tool output, persistence, and autonomous run-throttling semantics that automation cannot choose safely under the repo's compatibility and core-boundary rules.

options.title: Visibility-first provider pace
options.body: Expose provider quota windows and projected pace in status/session_status without blocking agent work until the UX and state model are validated.

options.title: Opt-in admission gates
options.body: Add disabled-by-default pace config for subagent or noninteractive admission, with explicit tests for both disabled and enabled modes.

options.title: Plugin/API boundary first
options.body: Expose any missing provider usage APIs and let a plugin or skill own policy until core maintainers choose default product behavior.

recommendation.title: Visibility-first provider pace
recommendation.body: Expose provider quota windows and projected pace in status/session_status without blocking agent work until the UX and state model are validated.

likelyOwner.reason: They have the clearest history on provider usage hooks and plugin/core boundary shape, which is the central decision here.
